blocks.text: Quick verdict

Webshare is the better value for steady monthly usage: 10 GB costs $27.50 against IPRoyal's $52.50, its 80M+ pool is larger, and the free datacenter tier makes integration testing painless. IPRoyal is the better choice for irregular workloads, because its residential gigabytes never expire while Webshare's allowance resets every 30 days, and for account management that needs sticky sessions longer than Webshare's 24-hour maximum. IPRoyal also offers mobile proxies, which Webshare does not.

IPRoyal and Webshare are both popular with developers and small teams, and both sell residential, ISP and datacenter proxies. The key difference is how bandwidth behaves. Webshare is cheaper per gigabyte but its monthly allowance resets every 30 days. IPRoyal costs more per gigabyte, but anything you buy stays in your account until you use it. Webshare also has a permanent free datacenter plan and a larger advertised residential pool. Here is how to decide which model fits your usage.

blocks.text: IPRoyal in 2026: what you get

IPRoyal built its reputation on flexible, non-expiring residential bandwidth and straightforward pricing. The pool is smaller than the enterprise networks at 32M+ advertised IPs, but it covers 195 countries, supports SOCKS5, and offers some of the longest sticky sessions available (up to seven days). Its headline $1.75/GB rate only applies at 10 TB; most buyers will pay between $5 and $7 per GB on small orders.

Strengths: Residential traffic that does not expire; Sticky sessions up to 7 days; Can start with a single gigabyte; Several proxy types plus Web Unblocker in one account. Weak spots: Smaller pool than the enterprise networks; Headline $1.75/GB rate needs a 10 TB purchase; Mid-volume prices are not published.
Webshare in 2026: what you get

Webshare is built for developers who want to configure everything themselves. Pricing is transparent, the free datacenter plan makes it easy to test integrations, and paid plans scale smoothly from tiny to large. Its residential network advertises 80M+ IPs across 195 countries. It does not sell mobile proxies or a broad scraping API, and paid plans start with an account-wide limit of 500 concurrent requests.

Strengths: Permanent free datacenter plan for testing; Low, transparent residential pricing; Excellent dashboard and API; Sticky sessions up to 24 hours. Weak spots: Bandwidth resets monthly with no rollover; No mobile proxies; 500-request default concurrency limit.
Pricing: IPRoyal vs Webshare

IPRoyal's residential subscription costs $7 for 1 GB, $11.90 for 2 GB and $52.50 for 10 GB ($5.25/GB); pay-as-you-go is 5% more ($7.35 for 1 GB). The advertised $1.75/GB rate applies only at 10 TB. Prices for custom volumes such as 25, 100 or 500 GB are calculated in the dashboard.

Webshare's rotating residential plans cost $3.50 for 1 GB, $27.50 for 10 GB, $65 for 25 GB, $225 for 100 GB and $875 for 500 GB per month, falling to $1.40/GB at 3 TB. Yearly billing is about 30% cheaper but is paid upfront for a 360-day term. Unused bandwidth resets every 30 days.

At 10 GB a month, Webshare is the cheaper option at about $27.50 against $52.50 for IPRoyal, roughly 48% less. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because IPRoyal does not publish an exact price for that volume; Webshare comes to about $225. The sticker price is only half of it. IPRoyal's unused traffic carries forward, while Webshare's does not (allowance resets every 30 days; no rollover), so if your usage swings from month to month IPRoyal can work out cheaper than the per-GB numbers suggest.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

By advertised size, Webshare (80M+) is about 2.5x larger than IPRoyal (32M+). Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, IPRoyal lists 195 countries and Webshare lists 195. On targeting, IPRoyal offers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification), while Webshare offers country, plus state, city or ZIP (US) or ASN.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, IPRoyal offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days, and Webshare offers rotating or sticky from 1 minute to 24 hours. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. IPRoyal: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls. Webshare: low prices and a developer-friendly API. Let price and the countries you need decide.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. IPRoyal: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product. Webshare: fine for light rank tracking. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: IPRoyal wins. The deciding factor for IPRoyal: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account. The limitation on the Webshare side: 24-hour sticky sessions and cheap static ISP IPs.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic. How Webshare compares: good for US work with ZIP targeting, thinner elsewhere.

Ad verification and geo-testing: IPRoyal wins. The deciding factor for IPRoyal: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts. The limitation on the Webshare side: no mobile network and limited selector combinations.

Tight budgets: Webshare wins. The deciding factor for Webshare: free tier plus some of the lowest per-GB rates here. The limitation on the IPRoyal side: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. IPRoyal: No general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. Webshare: 10 free datacenter proxies (1 GB/month); no residential trial. Verification and payment rules differ too. IPRoyal: Optional ID verification; required for ISP-level targeting and PayPal. Webshare: ID checks only when flagged or for restricted categories. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test IPRoyal and Webshare before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle IPRoyal vs Webshare faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (IPRoyal: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies; Webshare: 10 free datacenter proxies (1 GB/month); no residential trial).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, IPRoyal comes out ahead in 3, Webshare in 1, and 2 are ties. That makes IPRoyal the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: IPRoyal is strongest for irregular or seasonal projects, while Webshare is strongest for solo developers and small teams. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
